name: Boom Bap
blurb: 90s New York: dusty swung drums, jazzy keys, upright-style bass.
rules: Kick and snare on a swung 16th grid (swing 0.18 to 0.3); snare on 2 and 4; ghost snares and late off-beat kicks.
Minor 7th and 9th chords (i7 iv7, ii7 V7), changing every 1 or 2 bars; a short keys or horn-style riff on top.
Bass follows the chord roots with a few passing notes; no long 808 slides.
Arrangement: 4-bar intro with keys only, 8-bar verse, 8-bar hook with an extra layer, 8-bar verse, 4-bar outro.
example: Dusty boom bap, 90 BPM, D minor. Swung drums, jazzy Rhodes chords, walking bass, a short horn-style riff on the hook.

name: Atlanta Trap
blurb: Half-time trap: rolling hats, booming 808, dark melody.
rules: Half-time feel: clap/snare on beat 3 of each bar; kick follows the 808.
Hi-hats in 16ths with 32nd and triplet rolls at the end of every 2nd bar; an open hat now and then.
808 on the chord roots with octave jumps; long notes with short gaps.
Dark minor melody (bells, pluck or piano) in 4 bars; drop the drums for 2 bars before the second hook.
example: Dark Atlanta trap, 142 BPM, C minor. Rolling hats, booming 808 with octave jumps, bell melody, drums drop before the last hook.

name: West Coast G-Funk
blurb: Dr. Dre / Compton: synth whine lead, Moog-style bass, crisp snare and claps.
rules: One- or two-chord minor vamp (i7 iv7 or i bVII), harmonic minor allowed for a V chord.
Funky synth bass with octave pops and passing notes; a high sine-like whine lead playing long slides of notes.
Tight kick, crisp snare with clap on 2 and 4, 16th hats lightly swung (0.1 to 0.15).
Something new in each section: a piano figure in octaves in the verse, strings or a lead only in the hook.
example: West Coast G-funk, 94 BPM, E minor. Moog-style bass, high synth whine lead, piano in octaves, crisp claps.

name: Drill
blurb: Brooklyn / UK drill: syncopated snares, sliding-style 808 patterns, dark triplet melodies.
rules: Snare on beat 3 plus a syncopated extra snare late in every 2nd bar; kick sparse and matching the 808.
Hats skippy: x..x..x.x..x..x. with triplet rolls; no straight 16ths all the way through.
808 moves a lot: root, minor 3rd, octave, back down, with long and short notes.
Melody in triplets (beats 0, 0.67, 1.33) on piano, strings or choir; dark minor keys like C# or F# minor.
example: Brooklyn drill, 143 BPM, C# minor. Triplet piano melody, choir pad, skippy hats, moving 808, offbeat snares.

name: Neptunes Bounce
blurb: Pharrell-style: dry snappy drums, odd jazzy chords, big drop-outs.
rules: Very few sounds; dry, snappy snare and clap, tight kick, a 4-count stick or rim intro.
Extended chords (minor 9, add9, 7) played as short staccato stabs with gaps.
Hand-percussion-style fills (toms, rims, cowbell) answering the snare.
Hard drop-out: everything stops for 1 bar before the hook, then comes back at once.
example: Neptunes-style bounce, 100 BPM, E minor. Rim count-in, staccato minor 9 stabs, bucket percussion, a full drop-out before the hook.

name: Timbaland Rhythm
blurb: Stuttering kicks, ticking hats, sparse sounds, rhythm first.
rules: Syncopated stuttering kick pattern with 16th doubles (X..x..X.....x.x.); gated snare on 2 and 4.
Hats in fast triplets or 32nd ticks with gaps; percussion and vocal-sound hits as rhythm.
Only three or four melodic sounds; a short strange riff instead of chords.
Change the kick pattern in the hook (add stutters) rather than adding many layers.
example: Timbaland-style beat, 88 BPM, G minor. Stuttering kicks, ticking triplet hats, odd percussion, a short eerie synth riff.

name: Lo-fi Chill
blurb: Study-beat lo-fi: lazy drums, warm maj7 chords, soft piano.
rules: Lazy swung drums (swing 0.25 to 0.35), soft kick, rimshot or soft snare on 2 and 4, quiet hats.
Major 7 and minor 9 chords on piano or pads, one chord per bar; a gentle 4-note melody.
Low velocities (0.5 to 0.8) everywhere; nothing harsh; a short fade-in intro.
Arrangement loops calmly: intro 4, A 8, B 8, A 8, outro 4.
example: Lo-fi chill beat, 78 BPM, F major. Lazy swung drums, warm maj7 piano chords, soft pad, gentle melody.

name: Afrobeats
blurb: West African pop groove: off-beat shakers, log-drum style bass, bright guitar or keys.
rules: Kick on 1 and the 'and' of 2 (X.....x...X.....); snare or rim on the 3rd 8th of the bar and on 4.
Constant 16th shaker and off-beat percussion; a syncopated cowbell or clave pattern.
Bright major or Dorian chords (I vi IV V, i IV) on guitar or keys in short syncopated stabs.
Bass plays short bouncy notes that answer the kick; keep it danceable and steady.
example: Afrobeats groove, 106 BPM, A major. Off-beat shakers, clave pattern, bright guitar stabs, bouncy bass.

name: Reggaeton
blurb: Dembow rhythm, deep bass, minor plucks.
rules: Dembow drum pattern every bar: kick on 1 and 3 (X.......X.......), snare on steps 4, 7, 12 and 15 (....x..x....x..x).
Hats in 8ths; a short percussion fill every 4 bars.
Minor progression (i VI III VII) on plucks or a pad; bass on the roots in long notes.
Hook melody short and repetitive; drop the kick for 2 bars before the hook.
example: Reggaeton, 95 BPM, A minor. Dembow drums, deep bass, minor pluck melody, drop before the hook.

name: R&B Slow Jam
blurb: Modern R&B: lush chords, soft 808, finger snaps.
rules: Lush extended chords (maj7, min9, add9) on keys and pads, a chord every 1 or 2 bars.
Finger snap or soft clap on 2 and 4, gentle 16th hats with small rolls, soft kick plus an 808 on the roots.
A sweet melody line on keys or a synth, simple and singable.
Space for a vocal: verse thinner, hook with pads and a counter-melody.
example: Modern R&B slow jam, 70 BPM, Eb major. Lush maj7 keys, snaps, soft 808, sweet melody, pads on the hook.
